title: My Weird Little Jar of Bourbon Vanilla Tallow Balm (And Why It Works)
body:
Okay so I was scrolling on my phone, foot was asleep from sitting weird, and I saw this thing for a whipped tallow balm. Bourbon vanilla scent. Looked nice. Then I read the description. Beef fat. For your face. I just stared at my screen for a second. My brain went: *Putting steak juice on your cheeks? What?* That was my first, honest reaction. I mean, come on. It sounds bizarre. You’re telling me the secret to good skin is the same stuff they used to cook with in the 1800s? I almost scrolled right past. But my skin was being so difficult last spring—flaky, tight, just angry for no reason—and I’d tried the expensive stuff in the fancy jars. Nothing. So I was in that “fine, whatever, I’ll try anything” mood. I clicked buy. Figured the worst that could happen is I’d smell like a weird dessert and have to throw it out.

It showed up a while later. Small jar. Felt heavy for its size. I opened it sitting at my kitchen counter, the light was that weird yellow afternoon kind. Here goes nothing, right?

**How I Got Over the "Beef Fat on Face" Thing**

The mental hurdle is real. I get it. Beef tallow skincare sounds like a history lesson, not a beauty routine. You think of candles and old-timey cooking, not dewy skin. I had the jar for like, two days before I even touched it. Just sat there on my dresser. But then I started reading. Actually reading about it, not just skimming. And the thing is, it starts to make a weird amount of sense. Our skin produces its own oil, right? Sebum. Tallow from grass-fed cows is apparently really, really close to that. Closer than most plant oils or lab-made stuff. So the idea is your skin just… recognizes it. Knows what to do with it. It’s not a foreign substance it has to fight; it’s like giving it back something familiar it’s missing. That clicked for me. It’s not slapping a raw steak on your forehead. It’s this purified, whipped thing that’s mimicking what we already have. Or should have. When I put it like that, the whole “is tallow good for skin” question felt less crazy. It’s not magic. It’s just… compatible. In a very unexpected way.

So one night, after washing my face, I scooped a tiny bit out. It was cool. Solid but soft. I rubbed it between my fingers and it just… melted. Not like butter, but like it became a silky oil immediately. I braced myself for some gross farm smell. But it didn’t smell like beef. At all. It smelled like vanilla. But not like cake or cheap candy. Like a deeper, warmer vanilla. Bourbon vanilla, I guess. It was comforting. Cozy. Like the scent of a bakery at the end of the day, when things are quiet. I put it on my face. Here’s the weird part: it didn’t sit there. It just sank in. My skin drank it. I was expecting to be a greasy mess, but I wasn’t. It felt like nothing. But also like everything? Like my skin finally took a full breath after being held tight. I went to bed thinking, “Huh. That was… not what I expected.”

**What This Stuff Actually Did For My Spring Skin**

Spring is weird for skin. At least for mine. One day it’s warm, the next it’s windy and cold. My face gets confused. It was dry but also somehow rough in patches. I’ve had eczema on my hands before, and my cheeks were starting to get that same unhappy, tight feeling. I used this bourbon vanilla tallow balm that first night and woke up… fine. Just fine. Not miraculously transformed. But the tightness was gone. The rough patch by my chin felt softer. I kept using it. Morning and night. Just a little dab.

After a week, I noticed my foundation wasn’t clinging to dry flakes anymore. It just sat smooth. My mom, who never comments on that stuff, said my skin looked “rested” during a video call. I hadn’t slept well that week, so it definitely wasn’t that. It was the balm. The little fine lines around my eyes—the ones that look more obvious when I’m dehydrated—just seemed less… pronounced. Not gone. I’m not 22. But quieter. Like they decided not to shout that day. I started putting it on my hands too, because why not. The dry knuckles I always get? Gone in like three days. I’m not saying it’s a miracle cure for everything. But for dry, stressed, confused skin? It just works. It’s so simple it’s almost stupid. I got mine from this small shop on Etsy that makes it in France, and I keep thinking about how it’s just this one ingredient, whipped into this luxe texture, doing more than my 7-step routine ever did.

**Would I Buy This Tallow Balm Again?**

I’m on my second jar. That’s the answer. I ordered another one before I even ran out of the first. That’s how not-weird it is to me now. The “beef tallow skincare” mental block is completely gone. Now I just see it as this incredibly effective, simple moisturizer that smells nice and makes my skin happy. I told my sister about it. She made the same face I did. “Tallow? For real?” I just sent her the link and said “Trust me.” She got the unscented one. She texted me last week saying her elbows haven’t been this smooth since we were kids. So yeah.

It’s not for everyone. If you’re vegan, obviously, it’s a no-go. And if the idea just totally skeeves you out, that’s fine. But if you’ve tried a lot of things and your skin still feels dry or irritated, the benefits of a tallow balm are worth getting past the initial “huh?”. It’s one of those things that sounds primal and kinda gross until you realize it’s just skin taking care of skin, in the most direct way possible. My skin barrier feels stronger. It doesn’t freak out as easily. I don’t know how else to explain it.

**Quick Questions I Get Asked**

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, honestly. It sounds wild but it makes sense once you get past the idea. It’s very similar to the oils our own skin produces, so it absorbs deeply and helps repair the skin barrier instead of just sitting on top. It’s like giving your skin back something it knows how to use.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was worried about this too because my skin can get fussy. But no, for me it didn’t. Because it’s so similar to our sebum, it seems to absorb fully without clogging anything. It’s not like putting a thick, waxy layer on your face. It just melts in.

**What does the bourbon vanilla tallow balm smell like?**
It smells like vanilla, but not the sweet, ice cream kind. It’s warmer. Deeper. Like vanilla extract with a little something else that makes it feel cozy and kind of relaxing. It’s not overpowering at all. Fades pretty quick after you put it on.

Anyway. If your skin is being difficult and you’re curious, this might be worth a shot. It’s just a little jar of something that shouldn’t work but somehow does. I’m probably gonna order another one soon.
